title: Modelling and worldwide assessment of performance and aging of photovoltaic modules and systems
note: Primary scientific reference for this repository. University of Ljubljana catalogue: COBISS 77808131; national-library URN:NBN:SI:DOC-TMG3QFI9. Defended 21 September 2021. Marko Topič is the advisor, not a coauthor. No thesis DOI has been verified. Citation does not claim that every thesis chapter is implemented.
institution: University of Ljubljana, Faculty of Electrical Engineering

title: Typical Daily Profiles, a novel approach for photovoltaics performance assessment: Case study on large-scale systems in Chile
note: Source of the Typical Daily Profiles approach and original Chile fleet case study. Project qualification rules, missing-data handling, fixed-clock pooling and unavailable historical capacity gates are documented adaptations, not a claim of byte-identical author software.

title: Advanced PV Performance Modelling Based on Different Levels of Irradiance Data Accuracy
note: Source of the two-stage irradiance/power acceptance band and low/medium/high irradiance evidence levels. The repository states its interpretation of inconsistent printed roughness/distance expressions. Chronological validation and monotonic LightGBM settings are project adaptations.

title: Estimation of the diffuse radiation fraction for hourly, daily and monthly-average global radiation
note: Erbs decomposition through pvlib. Applying the hourly model at synthetic solar-position substeps is a declared integration approximation.

title: Calculations of the solar radiation incident on an inclined surface
note: Hay-Davies sky-diffuse transposition through pvlib. Metadata checked against pvlib documentation; no DOI is asserted. Ground reflection is handled separately by pvlib.
publication: Proceedings of the First Canadian Solar Radiation Data Workshop

title: Solar position algorithm for solar radiation applications
note: Solar position algorithm used through pvlib nrel_numpy. The twelve-substep integration and effective geometry selection are repository choices.

title: Fourier series representation of the position of the sun
note: Source of the Spencer Fourier approximation used by pvlib get_extra_radiation (its default method). The solar-position calculation itself uses the separate Reda-Andreas algorithm. Metadata checked against pvlib; no DOI is asserted.

title: Slope-Aware Backtracking for Single-Axis Trackers
note: Single-axis tracking/backtracking equations used through pvlib. The current geometry bank uses level cross-axis terrain; citing the general method does not assert surveyed slope or tracker configuration.

title: Tracking and back-tracking
note: Tracking/backtracking source cited by pvlib singleaxis, the implementation used by the geometry bank.
publication: Progress in Photovoltaics: Research and Applications

title: pvlib python: 2023 project update
note: Current project-level citation recommended by pvlib. Exact installed software versions are recorded in analysis manifests and the workspace lockfile.

title: Modeling with interval averages
note: Documentation motivating explicit interval alignment. The repository cosine-disaggregation scheme is its own approximation; this example is not a validation of that scheme.

title: LightGBM: A Highly Efficient Gradient Boosting Decision Tree
note: Original LightGBM algorithm reference. The optional model uses the LightGBM library; monotonic settings do not guarantee concavity or any minimum prediction score.
publication: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems

title: LightGBM parameters
note: Reference for deterministic CPU execution, objective compatibility, bounded thread counts and feature monotonicity. Version-specific behavior is tied to the lockfile.

title: Bounded-variable least-squares: an algorithm and applications
note: Bounded-variable least-squares algorithm selected explicitly as scipy.optimize.lsq_linear(method="bvls"). The nonnegative transformed PV basis and shape constraints are repository-specific. Author spelling verified against the author bibliography, correcting the typo in some SciPy documentation.

title: SciPy 1.0: fundamental algorithms for scientific computing in Python
note: SciPy provides the bounded least-squares numerical solver; see Stark and Parker for the chosen BVLS algorithm. This is not attribution of the repository-specific PV parameterization to SciPy.

title: IEC TS 63019:2019: Photovoltaic power systems (PVPS) - Information model for availability
note: Information-model context only. The ten observable states and numeric thresholds are project screening rules, not normative IEC categories or a conformity claim. Causes remain unconfirmed and the workflow does not compute certified availability.

title: Generación real: API de datos abiertos
note: Actual-generation API source. Use the exact request interval, access time, response provenance and effective unit roster recorded by the acquisition; catalogue inclusion is not evidence of live authorization or complete national coverage.

title: Infotécnica: registro público de centrales
note: Public plant registry source. Reported maximum power is retained without silently treating it as verified AC or DC nameplate capacity.

title: Reportes y estadísticas: generación del Sistema Eléctrico Nacional
note: Provider catalogue for historical generation and Qlik exports. Every imported export requires its specific source URL/file, timestamp conventions and hash; this general catalogue does not certify the completeness of a supplied export.

title: Generación real descargable (Qlik)
note: Source interface for preserved generation exports. The adapter imports user-supplied CSV/XLSX/ZIP exports with an explicit contract; citation does not imply anonymous live access, successful authorization or an implemented Qlik session client.

title: The ERA5 global reanalysis
note: Scientific description of ERA5 reanalysis. Reanalysis is modelled weather and cannot be relabelled as a measured station. Cite the actual dataset and acquisition wrapper separately.
publication: Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society

title: ERA5 hourly data on single levels from 1940 to present
authors: Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) Climate Data Store (CDS)
note: Single-level dataset citation as recommended by the Earthmover source catalogue. Record the actual retrieval date and selected data vintage; do not use the metadata-verification date as a data-access date.

title: Icechunk ERA5
note: Optional native ERA5 source. Cite Earthmover, the C3S single-level dataset, and underlying ERA5 research; acquisition must retain the pinned snapshot and actual access date. Catalogue metadata verification does not establish current snapshot coverage or a new data acquisition.

title: Historical Weather API
note: Optional ERA5 weather wrapper. Cite the underlying ERA5 dataset/paper and retain the explicitly requested product, grid cell and interval semantics; this is not measured irradiance.

title: Historical Forecast API
note: Optional archive of numerical forecasts. The adapter explicitly selects ECMWF IFS; do not describe these records as ERA5 or observations. Record model, vintage and interval semantics from provenance.

title: Weather Forecast API: hourly variable definitions
note: Provider definitions for preceding-hour radiation/gust variables and instantaneous temperature/wind. Archive-specific variable definitions take priority where products differ.

title: Overview of the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) experimental design and organization
note: Scientific design of the CMIP6 archive accessed by the retrieval provider. The repository retrieves published climate-model output; it does not implement or run the contributing climate models. Cite each selected model/experiment dataset and its version separately using the preserved provider citation links.

title: The Scenario Model Intercomparison Project (ScenarioMIP) for CMIP6
note: Scientific description of the SSP scenario experiments selectable by the CMIP6 retrieval provider. Scenario simulations are conditional climate projections, not observations or deterministic weather forecasts. Their availability and coverage are established by each saved catalogue result, not by this paper citation.

title: ESGF PyClient documentation: STAC migration and data-access services
note: Official access guidance identifies the east and west ESGF STAC discovery services and deprecates the legacy Solr search interface. This provider uses direct HTTP requests; this reference does not mean esgf-pyclient is a runtime dependency. Preserve the actual endpoint, search criteria, resolved dataset version, asset URLs and access time in acquisition provenance.

title: intake-esgf documentation: CMIP6 catalogue migration guidance
note: Upstream operational guidance documents CMIP6 republishing and inconsistent member identifiers in some STAC records. The retrieval implementation must preserve and validate identifiers instead of silently substituting another ensemble member. This reference is documentation, not a dependency or a claim of complete catalogue coverage.

title: STAC File Info Extension Specification, version 2.1.0
note: Defines byte sizes, relative local paths and hexadecimal multihash checksums carried by ESGF NetCDF assets. Checksums establish file integrity against the published asset metadata; they do not establish scientific accuracy or data completeness.

title: CMIP6 Guidance for Data Users
authors: Program for Climate Model Diagnosis and Intercomparison (PCMDI)
note: Document version 19 October 2022. Source of the data-citation and provenance guidance: retain official model and institution names, experimental identifiers, dataset versions and the original citation/further-information links. A general CMIP6 paper citation does not replace dataset-specific author and DOI attribution. Use the current STAC access documentation for endpoints because this older guide includes legacy interfaces.

title: CMIP6: Terms of Use, version 6.2
authors: Program for Climate Model Diagnosis and Intercomparison (PCMDI)
note: Document version 12 October 2022. Defines acknowledgement and data-citation requirements and directs users to the official per-model license inventory, which supersedes older file-header restrictions. Preserve source metadata and consult that inventory for data reuse; a catalogue-record license alone does not establish the license of the underlying model output or of this repository.

title: Baseline Surface Radiation Network (BSRN): structure and data description (1992–2017)
note: Canonical scientific description of the BSRN radiation archive. The provider retrieves station observations through PANGAEA and preserves their published identity and provenance. Cite the actual station collection and monthly dataset DOIs in addition to this network paper. Archive checks do not establish that a downloaded value passed every subsequent scientific quality check or represents a particular PV site.

title: Baseline Surface Radiation Network: Data retrieval via PANGAEA
authors: World Radiation Monitoring Center, Alfred Wegener Institute
note: Official source guidance for UTC timestamps, station/month datasets and logical records. The adapter targets basic radiation records; other record types require their own explicit contract. AWI states that resulting detailed BSRN quality-check flags are not archived. PANGAEA value annotations, when present, are preserved separately and do not establish completed scientific quality control. Preserve each dataset's citation, station metadata and BSRN data-release conditions.

title: PANGAEA Data Access and Reuse
authors: PANGAEA Data Publisher for Earth & Environmental Science
note: Documents DOI-based programmatic access, tab-delimited exports, structured metadata and citation links. PANGAEA describes these as standard HTTP access rather than a separate proprietary data API. The adapter retains the original citation/license text and source hashes; a DOI identifies the selected dataset and does not imply unrestricted access or a license for all PANGAEA holdings.

title: Global Historical Climatology Network-Hourly (GHCNh)
note: Official NOAA dataset citation, including all ten credited authors. Identify the actual station/year subset, product version and access date when citing an acquisition. The adapter retrieves GHCNh station reports and retains measurement, quality, source and report codes; the word hourly does not convert every reported value into a one-hour mean or supply missing irradiance observations.
institution: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information

title: Global Historical Climatology Network hourly (GHCNh): Documentation, version 1.1.0
authors: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
note: Official documentation updated 10 March 2026. Defines native station/year PSV access, station identifiers, units and measurement/quality/report/source codes. GHCNh version 1.1.0 supersedes previous versions and replaces the legacy ISD product. Preserve source fields and actual report timestamps; transformations into analysis intervals require a separately stated aggregation policy.

title: Service Location Change for Integrated Surface Data (Global Hourly)
authors: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
note: Official notice dated 23 June 2026 explains why new acquisition uses GHCNh. It records that legacy ISD updates stopped after 24 August 2025 and announces retirement of NCEI's ISD FTP/HTTPS distribution, while legacy files remain available through NODD. This repository's NOAA provider does not implement a legacy ISD fallback.

title: PANGAEA Quality flag definitions
authors: PANGAEA Data Publisher for Earth & Environmental Science
note: Defines numeric-value annotations for questionable, invalid, unknown, individually defined and inequality-qualified observations. The BSRN parser preserves the annotation and original field rather than silently treating an annotated value as unqualified. PANGAEA syntax alone does not certify detailed BSRN scientific quality control.

title: Basic measurements of radiation at station Cabauw (2009-06)
note: The explicit Cabauw June 2009 dataset used by the BSRN retrieval example. It is not a default station selection or an input to every analysis. Retain the retrieved dataset metadata, source hash and BSRN release conditions, and cite the associated station collection as well as this monthly dataset when using its measurements.
institution: Koninklijk Nederlands Meteorologisch Instituut, De Bilt

title: Basic and other measurements of radiation at station Cabauw (2005-02 et seq)
note: Station-level publication series containing the monthly Cabauw dataset in the retrieval example. The collection is updated over time; its citation does not assert that the entire collection was downloaded. Identify the exact monthly DOI and acquisition snapshot used, and preserve their associated station and instrument metadata.
institution: Koninklijk Nederlands Meteorologisch Instituut, De Bilt

title: AEMET OpenData API specification, version 2.0
note: Current official OpenAPI 3.0.1 document, service version 2.0. Defines header api_key authentication, daily-climate inventory and date-range endpoints, and recent conventional station observations described as the latest 12 hours. The recent endpoint does not accept a historical date range. Exact per-field units and observation periods are preserved from each retrieved metadata document.

title: AEMET OpenData: Frequently asked questions and two-stage data access
note: Official documentation of API estado responses and temporary datos/metadatos links, which expire after about five minutes. Field metadata contains source units, definitions, attribution and usage conditions. Canonical JSON snapshots retain data values and metadata; they do not claim to preserve exact HTTP encoding. Key expiry follows the newer published access notices rather than older FAQ PDF statements.

title: Interpretación: Hoy y últimos días
note: Official interpretation guidance distinguishing instantaneous temperature, wind averaging intervals, gusts and accumulated precipitation. The public website and API may display different units; this implementation checks returned API field metadata before assigning physical-unit columns. Native reporting dates and variable-specific aggregation periods are retained without inferring a uniform hourly observation contract.

title: AEMET OpenData: API access and key-expiration notices
note: Current 2026 notices describe retirement of keys issued without expiration and three-month validity for newly issued keys. The source reads AEMET_API_KEY from the environment, sends it through the documented private HTTP header and excludes credentials from output, provenance and public caches.

title: Hourly station observations of solar incoming (total/diffuse) and longwave downward radiation for Germany
note: DWD CDC dataset version v24.03; published 29 March 2024. Dataset identifier urn:x-wmo:md:de.dwd.cdc::obsgermany-climate-hourly-solar. CC BY 4.0. Native hourly radiation energy remains in J/cm², and acquisition hashes record the separately changing station-archive vintage.

title: DWD CDC dataset description: Hourly station observations of solar incoming (total/diffuse) and longwave downward radiation for Germany
note: Official version v24.03, published 29 March 2024 and last edited 6 May 2024. Defines native fields, hourly energy sums, missing sentinel -999, QN quality-procedure codes, true-solar-time labels, station metadata and CC BY 4.0. The adapter also verifies per-archive parameter metadata specifying UTC and WOZ; interval boundaries and irradiance flux are not inferred.

title: SURFRAD—A National Surface Radiation Budget Network for Atmospheric Research
note: Scientific network reference explicitly requested by NOAA in README_SURFRAD for publications using SURFRAD data. Author names and bibliographic fields verified against publisher-deposited Crossref metadata. Cite the actual station/day subset and access date as well. Page range follows Crossref and the NOAA README (2341–2357); the current AMS web display ends at 2358.
publication: Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society

title: An Update on SURFRAD—The GCOS Surface Radiation Budget Network for the Continental United States
note: Scientific network reference explicitly requested by NOAA in README_SURFRAD for publications using SURFRAD data. Author names and bibliographic fields verified against publisher-deposited Crossref metadata. Cite the actual station/day subset and access date as well. Describes the seven-station network and its BSRN affiliation; this affiliation creates potential overlap between archive routes.
publication: Journal of Atmospheric and Oceanic Technology

title: Description of SURFRAD Daily Data Files
note: Official 48-field native daily format, station filename aliases, UTC interval-end labels, three-minute averages before 1 January 2009 and one-minute averages thereafter. Defines missing sentinel -9999.9, native quality codes, physical units including UVB in mW/m² and instrument temperatures in Kelvin, and CC0-1.0 licensing. The provider preserves original flags and source values without additional filtering or correction.

title: SURFRAD Site Information
note: Official current station catalogue. The seven SURFRAD archive aliases are bon, tbl, dra, fpk, gwn, psu and sxf; Bondville has site code BND but file prefix bon. The separately linked ARM Southern Great Plains site is outside this provider. Current catalogue positions do not override historical file-header coordinates or elevations.

title: SURFRAD Overview: Surface Radiation Budget Monitoring
note: Official network scope, radiation and meteorological instrumentation, calibration context and BSRN participation. SURFRAD and BSRN archive acquisitions must not be treated as independent observations without checking station/time/variable/vintage overlap.

title: NOAA GML SURFRAD daily radiation and meteorological observations
note: Public GML station/year daily text archive actually used by this provider. Cite the selected station, UTC days and acquisition date; preserve its native files, quality flags and hashes. CC0-1.0 with NOAA attribution and fair-use guidance. This is not a claim to retrieve the separately published NCEI NetCDF, QCRAD, or realtime products.

title: BSRN Stations: PANGAEA station event catalogue
note: Official BSRN station inventory linked from the Alfred Wegener Institute station overview. Its bounded tab-delimited export preserves event codes, names, location, elevation, event dates, comments and source URIs. Event date extents do not establish monthly observation availability or continuous measurements; geographic proximity does not establish site representativeness. The selected catalogue and retrieval timestamp identify the acquisition vintage.

title: Methodology of Köppen-Geiger-Photovoltaic climate classification and implications to worldwide mapping of PV system performance
note: Fig. A1 classification precedence and fixed irradiation thresholds; Table 4 merges 24 raw combinations into 12 zones. Verified against the open-access institutional full text. Uses updated GPCC/CRU releases and caller-selected baseline rather than reproducing the original 1990-2016 map. Exact 18 C is assigned tropical, irradiation upper edges are inclusive, and aridity reductions use a machine-roundoff tolerance; these numerical conventions are explicit. No PV yield simulation is claimed.

title: World Map of the Köppen-Geiger climate classification updated
note: Eq. 2.1 seasonal dryness threshold uses at least two thirds of annual precipitation in winter or summer. The KGPV paper cites this work with year 2007, but the verified publication is 2006. KGPV Fig. A1 supplies the relabelling and polar/steppe equality rules.

title: GPCC Precipitation Analysis Monthly Version 2025
note: Four resolutions: 0.25, 0.5, 1.0 and 2.5 degrees. Cite the selected product DOI 10.5676/DWD_GPCC/MONTHLY_V2025_025, _050, _100 or _250 respectively; the request and retrieval manifest expose the exact DOI. Monthly totals; precip_infill is opt-in. Five-year blocks through 2020, 2021-2024 block, monthly files from 2025. Retain native gauge/error fields in raw archives. Follow DWD terms of use.
institution: Deutscher Wetterdienst, Global Precipitation Climatology Centre

title: Version 4 of the CRU TS monthly high-resolution gridded multivariate climate dataset
note: Method reference requested by the CRU TS provider. Data version is cited separately; use of this adapter does not imply that any particular analysis consumed CRU data.

title: CRU-TS Version 4.10
authors: Climatic Research Unit, University of East Anglia
note: Pinned release cruts.2604091129.v4.10, monthly 1901-2025 at 0.5 degrees over land excluding Antarctica. No version DOI was provided on the verified release page. Provider asks users to prefer CEDA and use UEA if CEDA is unavailable or the release has not yet been published there. ODbL with Database Contents License, attribution and share-alike. TMP is monthly mean temperature; PRE is monthly total; PET remains mm/day.

title: Xarray documentation: labelled arrays, CF decoding and interpolation
note: Software used for labelled climate grids, CF NetCDF masking/scaling, explicit coordinate alignment, interpolation and NetCDF serialization. The algorithms and scientific threshold choices remain attributed to their individual method papers.

title: Global Climate Data Processing and Mapping of Degradation Mechanisms and Degradation Rates of PV Modules
note: Source of climate-driven mechanism mapping and 0.2 percent/year categories, also presented in thesis Section 6.4. This implementation requires explicit module calibration and stress conventions. Mean daily extrema and arithmetic ambient humidity in the optional hourly processor are declared adaptations; the published global rasters and their calibration are not claimed reproduced.

title: Modeling Outdoor Service Lifetime Prediction of PV Modules: Effects of Combined Climatic Stressors on PV Module Power Degradation
note: Original hydrolysis, photodegradation, thermomechanical and multiplicative combined-rate equations (3)-(7), reproduced in thesis equations 3.14-3.17. Publication Boltzmann constant and normalization placement retained. Calibration and climatic aggregation must be supplied explicitly; no universal module coefficients, power-loss trajectory or service-lifetime predictor are implied.
